COUNTY BRIEF

Never a famous metal county — silver–lead–zinc lodes found ~1880 in the Stokes, Black Pine and Dolomite districts stayed small, and Snake River "flour gold" placers led the upper Snake 1902–15. The county's real mining industry is Oakley stone (micaceous quartzite, quarried since 1948, ~50,000 t/yr). The modern story is Black Pine: Pegasus Gold's open pit produced 435,000 oz Au (1991–97); Liberty Gold's oxide-gold project there holds a 3.11 Moz reserve, entered federal EIS permitting April 2026, and targets first gold in 2028 — which is why the southeast corner of the map is a wall of active claims. more ▾
